import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_67/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_67/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Join on 'user_id' as per operation history
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1[['user_id', 'city']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types
# Target schema: ['user_id': int, 'timestamp': str, 'source': str, 'device': str, 'operative_system': str,
#                 'test': int, 'price': int, 'converted': int, 'city': str]

# Convert types explicitly to match target schema
df_joined['user_id'] = df_joined['user_id'].astype(int)
df_joined['timestamp'] = df_joined['timestamp'].astype(str)
df_joined['source'] = df_joined['source'].astype(str)
df_joined['device'] = df_joined['device'].astype(str)
df_joined['operative_system'] = df_joined['operative_system'].astype(str)
df_joined['test'] = df_joined['test'].astype(int)
df_joined['price'] = df_joined['price'].astype(int)
df_joined['converted'] = df_joined['converted'].astype(int)
df_joined['city'] = df_joined['city'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target_columns = ['user_id', 'timestamp', 'source', 'device', 'operative_system', 'test', 'price', 'converted', 'city']
df_target = df_joined[target_columns]

# Write the final target table to the specified path without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform an outer join on 'user_id' to keep all rows from source0 and enrich with city info from source1
# The failed pipeline used inner join which caused too few rows (1228 vs 126352)
# Outer join will keep all source0 rows and add city where available
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1[['user_id', 'city']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Write the final output with exact target schema and column order
joined = joined[['user_id', 'timestamp', 'source', 'device', 'operative_system', 'test', 'price', 'converted', 'city']]

joined.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
